board.id: string, unique; becomes the value of `cli.js --board <id>` and of the `.components` manifest's "board" key
board.define: the preprocessor macro the application build gets (-D<define>); null for the default board, which is what libmbed.a is compiled with
board.svgAsset: the board drawing the viewer loads (null: not vendored yet)
board.pinGroups: ordered groups of pins; the first group may use expandPorts instead of pins
board.expandPorts: generates nameTemplate with {port}/{pin} for ports x pinFrom..pinTo, id = (port << idShift) | pin - the LPC1768 encoding, kept so the default board's values are unchanged
board.powerPads: pads with no PinName (GND, VBUS, RUN, ...), for T9's board rendering
board.onboardPeripherals: things soldered to the board (LEDs, buttons, the MCU itself), for T9's board rendering

pin.name: the name emitted in PinNames.h and (when `js`) in the JS map
pin.id: the pin's integer value - definitions only; unique per board
pin.alias: for an alias: the name of another pin in the same board, resolved transitively
pin.js: true = also emitted into the viewer's MbedJSHal.PinNames maps (default false)
pin.role: gpio | led | button | adc | console | nc | internal
pin.functions: alternate functions, transcribed from the SoC's Mbed CE pinmap
pin.physical: where the pad is: side (board-relative edge/block), pad (the pad's silk label), index (0-based position of the pad within that side; omitted when the order is not documented)
pin.onboard: id of the onboardPeripherals entry this pin drives
pin.note: free text, emitted as a comment in the generated header

powerPad.label: the pad's silk label
powerPad.physical: same shape as a pin's physical

onboardPeripheral.kind: led | button | mcu | memory | connector | debug
onboardPeripheral.label: the silk label / documentation name
onboardPeripheral.pin: the PinName it is wired to, or null when it is not driven by a GPIO
onboardPeripheral.svgId: the element id in the board drawing, e.g. "#led1"
onboardPeripheral.color: for LEDs: the colour the part lights up with

notes: Selected by passing no --board / --board default, and that is the branch libmbed.a is compiled with, so this block must stay reachable with no TARGET_BOARD_* define at all.

Every name here is a name of the pre-T8 hand-written PinNames.h with the same integer value; that is verified by compiling a probe against both headers and diffing the printed values (T8 evidence log).
The Mbed CE MBED_LPC1768 target says LED1..LED4 = P1_18/P1_20/P1_21/P1_23 and CONSOLE_TX/CONSOLE_RX = P0_2/P0_3, which is exactly what this board emits as LED1..LED4 and USBTX/USBRX.

CONSOLE_TX/CONSOLE_RX are deliberately NOT enumerators here: Mbed CE's hal/include/hal/PinNameAliases.h does `#define USBTX CONSOLE_TX` unconditionally, and platform.h includes it, so a TU can see the header with that macro live. Today the macro renames the USBTX enumerator, which compiles; adding a second enumerator literally called CONSOLE_TX would make that a duplicate-enumerator error.
The non-GPIO pads of the physical 40-pin DIP (p1..p4 and p31..p40, i.e. power and ground) are not modelled: the simulator's header has never named them and no demo or exercise references them.

The `#ifdef MCB1700` LED variant of the pre-T8 header is gone: MCB1700 is defined nowhere in this repository (grep: it appears only in that one #ifdef), so its branch was unreachable and LED1..LED4 keep the values of the branch that was always taken.

boards.mcu: Raspberry Pi RP2040 (dual Arm Cortex-M0+ @ 133 MHz)
notes: Mbed CE's own target for this board (mbed-os/targets/TARGET_RASPBERRYPI/TARGET_MCU_RP2/TARGET_MCU_RP2040/TARGET_RASPBERRY_PI_PICO/PinNames.h) names the GPIOs IO_0..IO_29 and defines LED1, I2C_SCL/SDA, SPI_SCLK/MOSI/MISO/CS and CONSOLE_TX/RX exactly as this board does; IO_n is kept as an alias so an application written against that target compiles here.

Pin ids are RP2040 GPIO numbers, except NC: nothing in the simulator's HAL decodes port << 5 | pin, it forwards the integer it was handed to MbedJSHal, so the id is free to be the GPIO number on this board.

physical.pad is the pad number printed on the board's 40-pin header (1..40); physical.index is that number minus one, i.e. the same 0-based position Mbed CE's PICO_P<n> aliases use - the PICO_P<n> aliases are copied verbatim from Mbed CE, which numbers them from zero.
GP25 drives the onboard LED. GP23, GP24 and GP29 are not pinned out (BUCK_REG_PWM_MODE, USB_VBUS_PRESENT, VSYS_MEAS).

The board has no GPIO-connected user button (BOOTSEL is tied to the flash chip select), so the standard BUTTON1 of the simulator's demos is wired to GP22 here: a real pad on the header, held down by the viewer's button on this virtual board.
LED2..LED4 do not exist on this board and are NC, which is Mbed's documented way to write DigitalOut on a board without that LED.

notes: Pin names and ids are Mbed CE's NUCLEO_F401RE target values (PA_0..PA_15 = 0x00..0x0F, PB_0..PB_15 = 0x10..0x1F, PC_0..PC_15 = 0x20..0x2F, PD_2 = 0x32, PH_0/PH_1 = 0x70/0x71, ADC_TEMP/VREF/VBAT = 0xF0..0xF2, NC = -1), so an application written against that target compiles unchanged.
PB_11 does not exist on the STM32F401RE; PB_12 is the next pad after PB_10.
D0..D15 and A0..A5 are Mbed CE's ARDUINO_UNO_D*/A* values for this board, i.e. the Arduino Uno header of the Nucleo.

physical.side is the functional block: 'arduino-digital' (D0..D15), 'arduino-analog' (A0..A5), 'arduino-power' (the power block), 'morpho' (ST morpho connectors only). physical.index counts within the block and is present only where the pad order is documented (the Arduino header); the ST connector designators (CN5/CN6/CN8/CN9) and the morpho pad order are deliberately not asserted here.
LED1/PA_5 is the user LED silkscreened LD2, verified in Mbed CE's own pinmap for this board ('Connected to LD2 [Green Led]'); LED2..LED4 do not exist as user LEDs and are NC.
BUTTON1/PC_13 is the blue user button B1 (Mbed CE's PinNames.h comment: 'B1 [Blue PushButton]').

I2C_SCL/I2C_SDA are PB_8/PB_9 (I2C1 on the Arduino header's D15/D14) and SPI_SCK/MOSI/MISO/CS are PA_5/PA_7/PA_6/PA_4 (SPI1), all taken from Mbed CE's PinMap_I2C_*/PinMap_SPI_* tables for this target. PA_5 is both the user LED and SPI1_SCK, exactly as D13 is on an Arduino Uno.
